result:
The proposed answer is incorrect for n ≥ 2. The error is in the claim that the generic centralizer in sp_{2n} has dimension n+1.

**Key observation.** Take x ∈ sp_{2n} with the form J alternating, so J^T = J in characteristic 2. The Lie algebra condition gives x^T J = Jx. By induction, (x^T)^k J = J x^k, so for any polynomial p, p(x)^T J = J p(x). Hence k[x] ⊆ sp_{2n} and k[x] ⊆ Z_{sp_{2n}}(x) for every x ∈ sp_{2n}.

**Regular elements exist.** For n = 2, take J = [[0, I],[I, 0]] and x = [[A, B],[C, Aᵀ]] with B, C symmetric. Choosing A = [[0,1],[0,0]], B = E₂₂, C = 0 gives x with x e₃ = e₄, x e₄ = e₂, x e₂ = e₁, x e₁ = 0. This is a single nilpotent Jordan block of size 4, so it is cyclic. Cyclicity is an open condition, so the generic x ∈ sp₄ is regular in gl₄. Then dim Z(x) ≥ dim k[x] = 4 for generic x, not 3.

**Consequence.** On a dense open set U ⊆ sp_{2n}, the fibres of the projection C₂(sp_{2n}) → sp_{2n} have dimension at least 2n. So dim C₂(sp_{2n}) ≥ n(2n+1) + 2n = 2n² + 3n. For n ≥ 2 this exceeds 2n² + 2n + 1, since 3n > 2n + 1 exactly when n > 1.

**Check at n = 1.** sl₂ in characteristic 2 has generic centralizer span(I, x) of dimension 2, giving dimension 5 = 2n² + 3n = 2n² + 2n + 1. So the proposed formula agrees only at n = 1, and the general argument (which relies on the quotient-by-centre reasoning in the proposed solution) does not hold in characteristic 2.

The argument above gives only a lower bound, 2n² + 3n. I did not verify that no stratum of non-regular elements contributes more, so 2n² + 3n is a likely but unconfirmed value of the dimension. What is established is that the proposed answer is too small for n ≥ 2.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
